recipes.name: Scandinavian-Style Rice Porridge
ingredients_raw: 8 whole green cardamom pods, lightly crushed to remove seeds, discarding pods
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, or amount desired

steps.text: Crush cardamom seeds with a rolling pin until very fine; place in a deep heavy pan. Add milk, rice, and 1 cup butter; cook over medium heat, while slowly stirring, for 90 minutes. Reduce heat if necessary to prevent milk from boiling or overheating. Stir in sugar; continue cooking until thickens, about 15 minutes more.
Pour rice mixture into a serving bowl. Add 3 tablespoons butter on top; let melt. Dust with cinnamon. Serve warm or cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Scandinavian-Style Rice Porridge
raw_recipe.description: This Scandinavian-style rice porridge recipe slowly cooks rice in milk and butter for extra-creamy, tender results. Cardamom and cinnamon add extra flavor.

review.reviewBody:
Just wanted to point out that this recipe is for Risengroet, not roemmegroet.
Roemmergroet is made with soured cream.

It is a OK recipe though, for risenrgoet.
I would skip the Cardamom pods and just add 1/4 tsp of ground cardamom if you really want the cardamom flavor. Risengroet usually does not have that flavor added. Some people add vanilla flavoring though.
I would also skip the sugar, as most people will want to add sugar to the top along with some butter and cinnamon.
Growing up in Norway this was a typical Saturday lunch:)

I’m sure this is divine made with whole milk, but I made several changes as I’ve learned that this recipe is very versatile - first, I made it with water and added splashes of almond milk as needed. I also made it using half white rice and half wild rice; I did not add sugar , and I used half butter/half coconut oil - I added several diced figs, and I simmered it 2 1/2 hours. It came out very creamy - I added a teaspoon of vanilla, and experimented in small bowls to see whether I liked a very small amount of molasses, or a very small amount of maple syrup - both were good, so I added a little of both to the pot. I topped the serving bowl off with a little half & half; it is absolutely delicious and healthy!
Turned out wonderful, I did make a few adjustments because I started with cooked rice but this was fantastic.
I'm a rice pudding lover! I thought this was a great recipe, although I'm not a huge fan of the cardamom flavor. It was lovely and creamy!
Yum. I made some substitutions and it was still great. I used nutmeg instead of cardamon, 3/4 c sugar and skim milk.
